Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

sgl_kernel_npu implements block verification for the chain-mode EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN rejection-sampling kernel, but the `--speculative-use-block-verification` gate in sglang rejects `device=="npu"`, so NPU users cannot enable it. This PR admits NPU for the chain path while keeping every other device's behavior unchanged.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`: allow `device=="npu"` in the block-verification gate for the EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN chain path only. and all other non-CUDA/ROCm devices are still rejected. The implicit enforcement of `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` (which strictly requires `--speculative-eagle-topk=1`) is unchanged.
- `arg_groups/fields/spec.py`: update the flag's help text to document NPU support.
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_block_verification_args.py`: add `test_supported_on_npu` (EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN accepted on NPU) and update the negative cases — DFLASH/DSPARK on NPU now hit the algorithm gate instead of the device gate, and cpu/xpu test the new device-gate message.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests: `test_block_verification_args.py` 5 passed (including `test_supported_on_npu`).

End-to-end on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NEXTN (NPU, TP2, `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-use-block-verification`, 6 fixed prompts):

- Greedy (temperature=0): all 6 outputs **byte-identical** to the classic chain-verification baseline (no block verification), with `avg_spec_accept_length` exactly equal (3.1167). This is the expected invariant: at temperature 0 the one-hot target distribution reduces Algorithm 2 to longest-argmax-prefix acceptance, i.e. classic greedy chain verification — so any deviation (or kernel failure) would be caught.
- Sampled (temperature=0.7): all 6 outputs deviate from the greedy baseline and `avg_spec_accept_length` stays at the same magnitude (3.12), confirming the sampled block-verification path is active and healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -120,7 +120,8 @@ class Spec(msgspec.Struct):
     speculative_use_block_verification: A[
         bool,
         "Use block verification for EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN (requires topk=1) or for "
-        "sampled DFLASH/DSPARK drafts, on CUDA or ROCm.",
+        "sampled DFLASH/DSPARK drafts, on CUDA or ROCm; on NPU only "
+        "EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN is supported.",
     ] = False
     speculative_token_map: A[
         Optional[str],

@@ -177,9 +177,17 @@ def handle_speculative_decoding(server_args: ServerArgs) -> None:
                 "--speculative-use-block-verification only supports EAGLE / EAGLE3 / "
                 "NEXTN / DFLASH / DSPARK."
             )
-        if cfg.device != "cuda":
+        if cfg.device == "npu":
+            # sgl_kernel_npu implements block verification only for the
+            # chain-mode EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN rejection-sampling kernel.
+            if cfg.speculative_algorithm not in ("EAGLE", "EAGLE3"):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "--speculative-use-block-verification on NPU only supports "
+                    "EAGLE / EAGLE3 / NEXTN."
+                )
+        elif cfg.device != "cuda":
             raise ValueError(
-                "--speculative-use-block-verification only supports CUDA or ROCm."
+                "--speculative-use-block-verification only supports CUDA, ROCm, or NPU."
             )
         # Block verification needs sampled proposals and their full distributions.
         # The DFLASH family's sampled drafts always carry them.

@@ -49,6 +49,21 @@ def test_supported_algorithms(self):
                         args.speculative_use_rejection_sampling, use_rejection_sampling
                     )
 
+    def test_supported_on_npu(self):
+        """sgl_kernel_npu implements block verification for the chain-mode
+        EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN rejection-sampling kernel."""
+        for algorithm in ("EAGLE", "EAGLE3", "NEXTN"):
+            with self.subTest(algorithm=algorithm):
+                args = self._args(
+                    device="npu",
+                    speculative_algorithm=algorithm,
+                    speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True,
+                )
+                handle_speculative_decoding(args)
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    resolution_result(args, "speculative_use_block_verification")
+                )
+
     def test_dflash_family(self):
         """DFLASH/DSPARK sampled drafts publish their own proposal distribution,
         so block verification must not switch on EAGLE's rejection sampling."""
@@ -90,16 +105,17 @@ def test_unsupported_configurations(self):
             ({"speculative_algorithm": None}, "only supports EAGLE"),
             ({"speculative_algorithm": "STANDALONE"}, "only supports EAGLE"),
             ({"speculative_algorithm": "NGRAM"}, "only supports EAGLE"),
-            ({"device": "cpu"}, "only supports CUDA or ROCm"),
-            ({"device": "npu"}, "only supports CUDA or ROCm"),
-            # DFLASH/DSPARK serve on NPU, whose chain sampler has no block mode.
+            ({"device": "cpu"}, "only supports CUDA, ROCm, or NPU"),
+            ({"device": "xpu"}, "only supports CUDA, ROCm, or NPU"),
+            # Block verification is unverified for DFLASH/DSPARK on NPU; only
+            # the chain-mode EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN sampler supports block mode there.
             (
                 {"speculative_algorithm": "DFLASH", "device": "npu"},
-                "only supports CUDA or ROCm",
+                "on NPU only supports EAGLE / EAGLE3 / NEXTN",
             ),
             (
                 {"speculative_algorithm": "DSPARK", "device": "npu"},
-                "only supports CUDA or ROCm",
+                "on NPU only supports EAGLE / EAGLE3 / NEXTN",
             ),
             ({"speculative_eagle_topk": 2}, "requires --speculative-eagle-topk=1"),
             ({"speculative_accept_threshold_single": 0.5}, "incompatible"),
